t.6.28.1: Those two, the king of men and the king of the monkeys, and that monkey, the son of Vāyu, and Jāmbavān, the king of the bears, and the rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa,
t.6.28.2: Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, Saumitri, the monkey Śarabha, Suṣeṇa together with his kinsmen, and Mainda and Dvivida as well.
t.6.28.3: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Kumuda, Nala, and Panasa as well, having reached the territory of the enemy, gathered together and deliberated.
t.6.28.5: Placing the accomplishment of the task foremost, take counsel together toward a firm decision, for Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, is ever present here.
t.6.28.4: Here is seen that city of Laṅkā, protected by Rāvaṇa, hard to conquer even by the immortals together with the Asuras, Uragas and Gandharvas.
t.6.28.6: While they were speaking thus, Vibhīṣaṇa, the younger brother of Rāvaṇa, spoke words rich in meaning and free of any vulgar expression.
t.6.28.7: Anala and Śarabha, and likewise Sampāti and Praghasa, my ministers, having gone to the city of Laṅkā, have come back here again.
t.6.28.8: Having all taken the form of birds, they entered the enemy's army, and having seen whatever arrangement had been made there, they have returned.
t.6.28.9: O Rāma, hear from me as I relate it all exactly as it is: the disposition of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa's forces, just as they have described it.
t.6.28.11: Indrajit, surrounded by many rākṣasas armed with paṭṭisas, swords and bows, and bearing spears and maces in their hands, holds the western gate.
t.6.28.10: Prahasta, with his army, has reached the eastern gate and stands there, and the mighty Mahāpārśva and Mahodara have taken their stand at the southern gate.
t.6.28.13: Rāvaṇa himself, deeply agitated and surrounded by many Rākṣasas, has taken his post, fully prepared, at the northern gate of the city.
t.6.28.12: The son of Rāvaṇa is surrounded by heroes bearing various weapons, by many thousands of rākṣasas with weapons in their hands.
t.6.28.14: Virūpākṣa, for his part, together with the rākṣasas and a mighty force armed with spears, swords and bows, has taken up his position at the central post.
t.6.28.15: Having observed such troop-stations as these in Laṅkā, all those ministers of mine quickly came back here again.
t.6.28.17: These night-rangers are valiant and mighty, fierce assailants with weapons raised in battles, and they are ever dear to the king of the Rākṣasas.
t.6.28.16: In the city there are a thousand elephants and ten thousand chariots, twenty thousand horses, and more than ten million rākṣasas.
t.6.28.18: Here, O lord of the people, for the purpose of battle, each single rākṣasa is attended by a retinue of a thousand thousands.
t.6.28.19: Vibhīṣaṇa told lotus-eyed Rāma, by way of reply, this news of the state of affairs in Laṅkā as his ministers had reported it.
t.6.28.20: When, O Rāma, Rāvaṇa fought against Kubera, then sixty hundred thousand rākṣasas marched forth.
t.6.28.21: Those here who, in valor, in prowess, in splendor, and by the greatness of their strength, are equal in pride to the evil-minded Rāvaṇa...
t.6.28.22: Do not be angry at this; I do not mean to provoke you or to frighten you, for by your valor you are able to subdue even the gods.
t.6.28.23: Therefore, surrounded by a great fourfold army and having arrayed this host of monkeys in battle formation, you will crush Rāvaṇa.
t.6.28.24: When Rāvaṇa's younger brother had spoken these words, Rāghava spoke these words for the purpose of repelling the enemies.
t.6.28.25: At the eastern gate of Laṅkā, let Nīla, the bull among monkeys, surrounded by many monkeys, be the one to oppose Prahasta.
t.6.28.26: And let Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, surrounded by a great army, assail Mahāpārśva and Mahodara at the southern gate.
t.6.28.27: Let Hanūmān, the son of the Wind, of immeasurable spirit, surrounded by many monkeys, assail the western gate and enter.
t.6.28.28: This petty one, fortified by the power of boons granted to him, delights in tormenting the hosts of Daityas and Dānavas and the great-souled sages.
t.6.28.29: He who roams through all the worlds, tormenting their creatures, that lord of the rākṣasas I myself am resolved to slay.
t.6.28.30: Together with Saumitri, I shall assail the northern gate of the city and force my way in, where Rāvaṇa stands with his army.
t.6.28.31: Let the mighty lord of the monkeys, and Jāmbavān, king of the bears, and also the younger brother of the lord of the rākṣasas, be stationed in the central division of the army.
t.6.28.32: Indeed, no human form is to be assumed by the monkeys in battle; let this be our sign of recognition in this war, within the monkey army.
t.6.28.33: The monkeys themselves will be our mark of identification among these our own people, but we seven shall fight the enemy in human form alone.
t.6.28.35: Having thus spoken to Vibhīṣaṇa for the accomplishment of his purpose, that wise Rāma set his mind and resolve upon ascending Mount Suvela.
t.6.28.34: I myself, together with my brother Lakṣmaṇa of great might, and this friend of mine, Vibhīṣaṇa, who is himself the fifth with his companions.
t.6.28.36: Then the great-souled Rāma, covering the whole earth with his mighty army, advanced upon Laṅkā with a joyful countenance, that great-souled one having set his mind on the slaying of his enemy.
